title: fix(superheroes): a merge sheet accounts for every acceptance its PR bodies list
body:
Closes #2092.

## What's changing, and why

A PR or stack merge sheet can no longer say "Nothing. The review left nothing for you." while a PR it covers lists acceptances. The sheet still holds only the items the advisor curated, under your "91 a" rule, and nothing is turned into a card automatically.

`pr_sheet.py build` reads each covered PR's body. You give it one `--pr-body <number>=<file>` per PR, and it refuses to build without them. The advisor's input then has to account, in a new `accounting` map, for every acceptance listed under the body's `## What we're accepting` heading. Each acceptance goes to exactly one of four places:
- its own Accept item;
- a line of the one "What you're accepting" fold;
- the leftover card it restates;
- the Canon entry the summary cites.

The build refuses a sheet that leaves one out, counts one twice, or points at an item, fold line, leftover or Canon id that is not there, and each refusal names the bullet. No body bullet becomes a card on its own. Each acceptance's id comes from its own text, so when an author adds a new acceptance above the others, only that one new bullet needs an entry.

The "nothing to accept" wording appears only when the build recorded that every covered body lists none. That covers the page's line, the app-bar count, the chat prose and the index row. Otherwise the sheet says it was "not checked against the PR body".

## What we're accepting

- **The advisor's sheet input grows.** Every acceptance the PR bodies list needs an `accounting` entry. A first build without one lists every bullet's id and text, so the advisor copies the ids from that refusal. TRANSITION says so under `## Unreleased`.
- **A sheet whose acceptances are all covered by Canon rulings reads "not checked against the PR body", not "nothing to accept".** The check did run in that case; the line still sends you to the PR body rather than claiming there is nothing. Giving that case its own accurate line needs a new sheet state, so it goes to the advisor (FU6). The review record holds it as a leftover for you (two Minor findings).
- **One leftover in the review record is already fixed.** A round-2 finding that a fold naming an item with no `ifLeft` crashed the build was raised at a second place in the code. It is the same defect as the fold-crash finding fixed in `e81759c`, and a test now covers it. The loop had already ended and did not merge the two, so the record still asks you to decide on it (FU8). Together with the two Canon-only findings, the record reads `not-reviewed` until you or the advisor settle the three.
- **The body reader is still a small line scanner, not a full Markdown parser.** This leg fixed four more edge cases that could hide an acceptance (text between two comments, a code fence inside a list item, a tab-indented closer, a fence that outlives its list). On a body it cannot read, it still fails toward showing a bullet rather than hiding one.
- **The PR grew past its size line.** It is 359 non-test lines (334 by the bar count) against an estimate of 150. The advisor ruled to keep it as one PR, recorded on #2092.
- **The review finished as an audited chain, not a fresh full panel.** Round 1 was the full panel plus a gap sweep. Rounds 2–4 audited each fix and ran a scoped finder. Every seat ran on Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, outside the makers' family. As before, the PR-body grounding seat did not run, because the review loop has no phase for it (FU5).
- **Four disclosed degradations** (build record below): an implementer order stopped partway on a cold offline cache, the host model was unknown to the seat composer, the grounding seat did not run, and no second brief-check ran on the fix-leg design (the advisor accepted it instead).

## How to see it

N/A — say it: this is plugin library and page code with no running app. The tests, the bite-proofs and the review are the check.

## Advisor vet
<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · aaa837c8316254835754a96cbadf86a0684493b0

**What was checked.** Your "1 a" is in: a merge sheet now has to account for every acceptance its PR bodies list, and it still curates them your "91 a" way. Each acceptance is its own card, a line in the one "What you're accepting" list, the leftover card it restates, or skipped with a Canon ruling. I ran it on #2075's real body. Without accounting it refuses and names all 8 acceptances; with it, it builds the same 5 cards you answered on that sheet. A sheet that leaves one out, counts one twice or points at nothing is refused, naming the acceptance. A body that lists none still says "nothing to accept". CI is green.

**What accepting it means.** I write a small accounting map for every sheet from now on; the build hands me the ids. One rare case reads wrong: a sheet whose acceptances are all covered by Canon rulings says "not checked against the PR body" when it was checked. The sheet asks whether to fix that now or in a follow-up.

**What is yours to decide.** Two cards on the sheet: that rare "not checked" line, and a fold-crash finding the review left for you that is already fixed (I confirmed it).

Receipt: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2093#issuecomment-6376238523

**Fix leg (vet 617 V617-1, the owner's "1 a").** A fresh cloud session built this leg on its own branch `claude/workhorse-issue-2092-0u7vfl`. It fast-forwarded this PR's branch on the advisor's written answer to the builder note ([issue comment](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2092#issuecomment-6372620245)); there was no force-push. `main` had not moved since `9464afc`, so the bring-current step was a no-op.

**Brief:** [issue comment](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2092#issuecomment-6367920564). The brief-check dispositions are in [this comment](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2092#issuecomment-6368052752).

**Brief change log:**
- 2026-10-23, fix leg: the shape changes from body cards to curated accounting. The input gains `accounting` (keyed by a content-derived bullet id; each value is exactly one of `{item}`, `{fold, line}`, `{leftover}` or `{canon}`); body bullets make no cards; the `a-` cross-check goes.
- The design was posted on #2092 ([builder note](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2092#issuecomment-6372680424)). The advisor accepted it as written and ruled "continue" on size.

**Why the id is content-derived:** a bullet's id is `<PR>:<10 hex>` over the PR number, the bullet's text and its place among identical texts. An acceptance inserted above others leaves every other id unchanged, so the accounting already written stays right (FU1).

**Review record:** https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2093#issuecomment-6374599539. It reads `not-reviewed` for three reasons:
- the two Minor Canon-only wording findings (my out-of-scope ruling routes them to the advisor as FU6);
- the already-fixed fold-crash duplicate (FU8).

The earlier record's carried leftover (FU1, duplicate-ordinal identity) is marked fixed, on the driver's own re-check.

### Follow-ups for the advisor

Worth a plugin surface: warm the uv cache before the first claude write dispatch in a cloud session.
